name: 22-down-into-mt-moon
objective: Out of the Mt Moon Pokemon Center, into the mountain's west mouth, across the first floor and down the ladder to B1F. The goal is B1F rather than the cave mouth because arriving on 1F is not a milestone: which of its three ladders is taken decides the whole rest of the crossing.
evidence: map=0x3C - wCurMap $D35E. MT_MOON_B1F is const index 60, and the warp graph read out of the maps' own object data names it: Route 4's warp[1] at (18,5) leads to map $3B warp[0] at (14,35), and map $3B's warp[3] at (17,11) leads to map $3C warp[2] at (25,9).

THE THREE LADDERS DOWN ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, which is why the route names one. Map $3B's warps [2],[3],[4] at (5,5), (17,11) and (25,15) land on map $3C at (5,5), (25,9) and (25,15), and those three tiles are in three pockets of B1F that do not connect to each other on foot: x=4-7 rows 4-17 plus row 16-17 out to x=21; x=14-25 rows 8-11; and x=24-27 rows 14-27 plus row 26-27 back to x=10. The exit from the mountain, warp[7] at (27,3), is in a FOURTH pocket - x=20-27 rows 2-3 - which no 1F ladder reaches at all and which is entered only from B2F, through B1F's warp[6] at (23,3). So every crossing of Mt Moon is 1F to B1F to B2F and back up to B1F.

This ladder is the shortest of the three by breadth-first path over the cartridge's own walkability grid: 40 steps from the entrance against 53 for (5,5) and 41 for (25,15), and its B1F pocket's own way down to B2F - warp[1] at (17,11) - is 10 steps from where it lands, against 28 and 24 for the other two.

THE WALKABILITY GRID NEEDED A SECOND TABLE BEFORE THIS ROUTE COULD BE DRAWN AT ALL. Gen 1 keeps TilePairCollisionsLand beside each tileset's collision list: three-byte records of (tileset, tile, tile), terminated by $FF, naming pairs that are each walkable on their own and that the game refuses to let you step between - CheckForTilePairCollisions in home/overworld.asm reads it. Its first record is CAVERN, $20, $05, found in this cartridge at file offset 0xC7E by that record's own bytes, which occur exactly once. Mt Moon 1F's one-tile corridor at x=9 is $05 and the floor beside it is $20, so a grid built from the collision list alone offers a route straight through it: measured, 53 of 60 attempts stuck within four tiles of it, the solver pressing left into a wall. Viridian Forest's tileset has six entries of its own, so any cave or forest route drawn here needs this table.

The route turns north at x=31 rather than x=30 because the LASS at (30,4) faces down and her cone runs along column 30: a walker that climbs it is stopped inside it, and TrainerWalkUpToPlayer then parks her body on the tile above, sealing the climb. One tile east and she is engaged from row 7 or row 10 instead and parks on a column neither leg uses - the same rule link 20's row-4 crossing is the fourth instance of.
